subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Rabindranath Tagore and Indian Short Fiction
description: A fast breakdown of Rabindranath Tagore and Indian Short Fiction for builders.

hook.text: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in 1913 and became the first non-European laureate in literature.

buildup.text: His Bengali short stories explored rural India with empathy, focusing on women, children, and the marginalized.

discovery.text: In Kabuliwala, a fruit seller from Afghanistan befriends a little girl who reminds him of his own distant daughter.

twist.text: Tagore returned his knighthood to the British in 1919 to protest the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of unarmed Indians.

climax.text: He proved that short fiction in a non-European language could achieve the highest international recognition.

punchline.text: He won the world's praise, then rejected its honors.

quiz.question: Why did Tagore return his British knighthood?
options: He preferred to use his Bengali title instead
To protest the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of unarmed Indians
He was forced to by the Indian independence movement
